one_liner: Experimental io_uring recursive file copier for Linux, about 2-3x faster than GNU cp -r on the author's NVMe box.
what_it_does: wcp is a command-line replacement for `cp -r SRC DEST` that copies a single file or a directory tree and shows a progress bar with ETA, counting the total size in parallel with the copy. It takes exactly two arguments (no flags, no multiple sources) and handles regular files, directories and symlinks. It is a tool, not a library, although the CMake build also produces a wcp_lib static library.
how_it_is_fast: All reads and writes go through io_uring (bundled liburing) as linked read-then-write submissions (IOSQE_IO_LINK), so many files are in flight at once without a syscall per operation, and directory walking runs alongside the copying. Source files are opened with O_DIRECT, which bypasses the page cache on reads, into one large aligned buffer pool of max(RAM/10, 1 GiB) split into 128 MiB blocks. The author's own summary is 'a lot of CPU, as much RAM as I can get away with, and 100% non-portable'.
when_to_use: Bulk copies of many small files (thousands to hundreds of thousands of 1 KiB-1 MiB files) on a fast NVMe SSD under Linux 5.6+, where cp's per-file synchronous syscalls dominate
Large sequential copies (hundreds of MiB per file) where the author measured about 2.1x cp's throughput
One-off interactive copies where an accurate progress bar and ETA matter
As reference code for an io_uring copy pipeline (linked read/write SQEs, O_DIRECT alignment handling) to build into your own tool
when_not_to_use: Anything needing cp's options: no -p/-a, so ownership, timestamps and xattrs are not preserved, and there are no flags at all
Production or scripted use: the author says it is probably not robust enough for daily use, issue #14 (named pipes break it) is open, and earlier issues reported segfaults and SIGTRAP
Non-Linux systems, kernels older than 5.6, or older distributions (open build failures on CentOS 7.4 and Debian, issues #12 and #10)
Memory-constrained machines: it allocates at least 1 GiB (10% of physical RAM) of copy buffers up front
Other hardware: open issue #13 reports wcp slower than cp on Ubuntu 20.04.1 AMD64

integration.form: CLI tool (CMake build; also a wcp_lib static library)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (the record's language field says C, but the code is C++17), CMake 3.11+, Linux kernel 5.6+ (tested on 5.8)
integration.platforms: Linux only (x86-64; ARM build fixed in issue #9)
integration.thread_safety: not applicable (standalone process); not documented for wcp_lib
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it covers `cp -r SRC DEST` for one source with default semantics only, with no options

gotchas: No fsync anywhere in the source: destination writes are buffered, so timings with 64 GB RAM partly measure filling the page cache (cp -r does not fsync either); the README does not say whether caches were dropped between runs, and wcp's O_DIRECT reads skip a warm source cache that cp could use

The 200,000 x 1 KiB row reports 200.51 MiB/s, but 200,000 KiB in 3.92 s is about 49.8 MiB/s (derived from page data); the files/s and seconds columns agree with each other, so the MiB/s column for small files looks inflated, probably by counting padded O_DIRECT block sizes
The README headline 'up to 70% faster' understates its own table (2.1-3.1x on wall time, derived from page data)
Errors in source files (FIFOs, unreadable files) are reported but can stop the status display (issue #14)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: liburing is the io_uring library wcp is built on; pick wcp when you want a ready-made copier, and liburing when you are building your own I/O path. parallel-disk-usage is the same kind of parallel tree-walk speedup applied to du, not to copying.
verified_claims_summary: On the author's machine (64 GB RAM, Samsung NVMe SSD, Linux 5.8, CPU and compiler not stated, CMake Release build), wcp copied 20 x 512 MiB files in 3.97 s vs 8.44 s for cp -r, 7,000 x 1 MiB files in 2.64 s vs 8.29 s, and 200,000 x 1 KiB files in 3.92 s vs 9.23 s (rsync 8.09 s). There is no benchmark script, the page-cache state is not stated, and an independent user (issue #13) saw it slower than cp.
status_note: Abandoned since 2021-05-21 (issues from 2021-2024 left open) but MIT-licensed and about 1,500 lines of C++, so small enough to read or vendor as a reference io_uring copy pipeline.
